parsed_answer.content: When Java 8 introduced Lambda Expressions, the compiler team opted against generating anonymous inner classes for every lambda. Doing so would have bloated the metaspace and generated thousands of class files at build time, leading to significant cold-start performance penalties. Instead, the Java compiler uses the 'invokedynamic' (indy) instruction, introduced in JSR 292, to defer the binding of the lambda implementation until runtime. When the JVM encounters an invokedynamic instruction for a lambda, it calls a 'bootstrap method' (BSM) provided by the JDK's LambdaMetafactory. This factory dynamically generates a class at runtime that implements the target functional interface, effectively acting as a bridge between the functional call site and the actual method body.

items: The compiler transforms the lambda body into a private static method within the enclosing class, effectively performing 'lambda lifting'.
The invokedynamic instruction points to a constant pool entry that specifies the bootstrap method, the target method handle, and the functional interface signature.
LambdaMetafactory caches the generated class, ensuring that subsequent calls to the same lambda expression reuse the same class definition, minimizing overhead.

Capturing lambdas (those that reference local variables) require the LambdaMetafactory to pass those captured values as arguments to the generated class constructor, whereas non-capturing lambdas are often stateless and can be cached as singletons.

parsed_answer.content: A common production trap is assuming that lambdas are always 'free'. While they avoid the overhead of explicit class files, they still involve a one-time cost for the LambdaMetafactory to generate the class and link the call site. Furthermore, if you are using reflection or heavy serialization, lambda-generated classes can sometimes cause unexpected 'IllegalAccessError' exceptions or issues with frameworks that expect concrete class names, as these generated classes exist only in the JVM's memory and do not have a physical .class file on disk.
